stories.label: 'Do you support demand for free Kashmir?' BJP questions Congress over MP Imran Masood's Jamia visit amid student protests
stories.summary: Students at Jamia Millia Islamia, a historically Muslim university, are protesting and on hunger strike, among their demands the release of Sharjeel Imam, jailed without trial since 2020 in the Delhi riots case. The ruling BJP has turned a Congress MP's visit into a 'free Kashmir' loyalty test. Lead with how long Imam has been held untried and what the students are asking for, then the mechanism: dissent at a Muslim institution recast as separatism. Datelined New Delhi.

stories.label: Ebola: Lagos is prepared to respond -- Commissioner
stories.summary: Continues the Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak in Nigeria, which Africa CDC says is underestimated. The development: Lagos, a city of over 20 million and West Africa's main air and sea hub, has activated its emergency operations centre around a confirmation. Lead with exactly what was confirmed and where, per the source; then the stakes: Bundibugyo has no licensed vaccine or approved treatment, and a case in Lagos means the outbreak can travel. Name the commissioner, Akin Abayomi, and what is in place: surveillance, isolation, testing.

stories.label: Jio IPO sets records with Rs 30,188 crore issue, draws Rs 7.4 lakh crore in bids: Check highlights
stories.summary: Jio Platforms' Rs 30,188 crore IPO, India's largest, drew Rs 7.4 lakh crore in bids, about 25 times the issue, and was covered within 100 minutes, while foreign investors were heavily selling Indian stocks. Lead with that contrast: domestic money absorbing a record listing as foreign money leaves. The structural point is Reliance's (Mukesh Ambani's) control of India's largest telecom and digital platform, now with public shareholders. Datelined Mumbai.

stories.label: Kazakhstan Cuts Base Rate by 50 Basis Points as Inflation Slows
stories.summary: Kazakhstan's central bank cut its base rate by 50 basis points as inflation slowed. Lead with the new rate and the inflation figure behind it. The mechanism: an oil exporter easing while Brent crude is above $110 because of the Iran war, meaning the windfall from the war is letting Astana cut where oil importers cannot. Albania's core inflation falling to 2.37% (Bank of Albania) is the same disinflation in another economy and can serve as a line of context, not the lead. Datelined Astana.

stories.label: UAE's Ras Al Khaimah closes beaches amid regional oil spill
stories.summary: Ras Al Khaimah has closed all its beaches until further notice after an offshore oil leak, and neighbouring Sharjah and Umm Al Quwain have imposed their own restrictions. Lead with the spread across three emirates. Then what is exposed: Gulf states drink desalinated seawater, so a slick near intakes is a water-supply risk as well as a hit to fisheries and tourism. Say what the source reports about where the oil came from; if it ties the leak to a tanker or to the attacks on shipping near Hormuz, say so, and do not assume it.

stories.label: A 1,000-mile cloud on Mars may reveal physics never seen in nature
stories.summary: Each Martian spring and summer morning a thin cloud forms over the volcano Arsia Mons and stretches up to 1,000 miles before vanishing. A new model says it may form ice in a way never directly observed anywhere. Lead with the cloud's scale and daily rhythm, then the proposed physics: what is different about how ice nucleates in that thin, cold air. Name the researchers and the journal from the source.

stories.label: An Ancient Virus Explains Why the Human Brain Is Special
stories.summary: Scientists found a family of retroviruses that invaded the genomes of chimpanzees and other primates and silenced genes involved in brain development, while the human lineage escaped it. Lead with the reversal: part of what sets the human brain apart may be an infection our ancestors avoided, not a gain. Name the genes, the study and the journal from the source.

stories.label: Ice sheet expansion may have started 2,000 years ago, but we canceled that
stories.summary: Barnes Ice Cap on Baffin Island, the last fragment of the Laurentide Ice Sheet that once buried most of North America, began growing around 2,000 years ago as the Earth's orbit cooled the Arctic. A new study says human warming has reversed that. Lead with the finding that the natural slide toward glaciation had begun and was undone, and the evidence (dated moss emerging from under the ice). Datelined Baffin Island.

stories.label: 祭出 Kosmo，禾赛要成为机器人的博世？
stories.summary: Hesai, the Chinese lidar maker that leads the world in car sensors, has launched Kosmo, a sensing product for robots, aiming to become the 'Bosch of robotics': the component supplier behind every maker rather than a robot maker itself. Lead with what Kosmo is and what it costs or does, then the strategy: China's humanoid and service-robot boom needs cheap perception at volume, and the supplier of that layer captures the industry. Take the inside view of the Chinese tech press. Datelined Shanghai.

stories.label: U.S. crypto delays hand digital asset advantage to Asia and Middle East, says Apex Group CEO
stories.summary: With the US Clarity Act, the market-structure bill for digital assets, stalled, tokenized money-market funds and regulated yield-bearing stablecoins are being built in Asia and Gulf hubs such as Abu Dhabi, Dubai and Singapore instead. Lead with the bill's failure and what it leaves unregulated in the US, then the mechanism Apex Group's Peter Hughes describes: tokenized funds used as collateral. Attribute the claim of lost business to him, and give the Gulf regulators' rules as the concrete alternative.

stories.label: Ukraine plans independent satellite system as Starlink issues persist
stories.summary: Kyiv says its military Starlink/Starshield link is 'stable' again after a roughly 10-day disruption, and is now planning its own satellite system. Lead with the dependency: a country's frontline communications ran through one foreign billionaire's network, and a 10-day outage was enough to push Kyiv toward sovereign infrastructure. Explain what an independent constellation would take (cost, years, launch capacity) and who else in Europe is chasing the same.

stories.label: Vow of revenge from King Abdullah II after church attack in Jordan
stories.summary: New development since our seven-dead report: the toll rose to eight when a wounded woman died, the government has formally called the Karak Orthodox church shooting a terrorist attack, and King Abdullah visited in military uniform vowing the gunmen will pay. Lead with the toll and the designation; explain what Jordan's security tightening means for its Christian minority and for a kingdom already strained by the Gulf war on its borders.

stories.label: North Korea's Kim Jong Un visits China via newly opened bridge
stories.summary: Kim crossed into Dandong by train over the New Yalu River Bridge — a span finished years ago but left unopened — on his first known trip abroad in over a year. Lead with the bridge as the signal: opening the main trade artery between the two states says Beijing is ready to deepen economic ties with Pyongyang despite sanctions. Note the timing, days before China's Fifth Plenum.

stories.label: Seven missing after tall building collapses in Kenya's capital
stories.summary: A 16-18 storey block in Nairobi's Eastleigh pancaked from the ground floor up; seven are feared trapped and police fired tear gas at looters. Lead with the accountability question: Nairobi has a long record of collapses of buildings that went up without approved plans or past stop orders. Name who approved this one and what Governor Sakaja's county has done about unsafe high-rises.

stories.label: Neha Bora refuses to sign peace bond, questions curbs on dissent
stories.summary: Delhi Police are using colonial-era 'peace bond' notices — a magistrate's demand that protesters post surety to keep the peace — against student and opposition activists; AISA president Neha Bora refused to sign after the Delhi High Court ruled, and CJP's Saurav Das faces a peace-bond violation case. Lead with the mechanism: a preventive tool that punishes protest before any offence, and what the court actually decided.

stories.label: Chart of the Week: French government and corporate bond yields are converging
stories.summary: Investors now charge the French state about what they charge French companies to borrow — normally a government is the risk-free benchmark. Lead with that inversion of the usual order and its cause: political instability and deficits, as mass protests shut Paris metro stations this weekend. Explain who pays — higher debt service crowding out public spending.

stories.label: Meta迎来“分裂季”
stories.summary: Meta's free cash flow has turned negative for the first time since its IPO, as AI data-centre spending outruns the ad business. Lead with that number and the capex figure behind it; the mechanism is the AI arms race converting the most profitable ad machine into a cash burner, read from the Chinese tech press's vantage.

stories.label: Deepseek招天才，Kimi找老兵
stories.summary: China's two leading open-model labs are hiring in opposite ways: DeepSeek recruits young prodigies, Moonshot's Kimi seasoned veterans — a contest between compute scale and talent density. Lead with the concrete hiring moves and pay, and what each bet says about how Chinese labs compete under US chip controls; this follows our Kimi K3.1 and DeepSeek DeepInfer coverage.

stories.label: NASA Outlines the Details of Artemis III and IV Missions
stories.summary: NASA laid out the mission plans for Artemis III (2027) and IV (2028), still aiming to land astronauts on the Moon in 2028. Lead with what changed in the mission design and which pieces (lander, suits) the timeline depends on, set against China's crewed lunar target of 2030.

stories.label: Argentina drops investigation into Milei over crypto fraud
stories.summary: A criminal investigation into President Javier Milei and his sister Karina over the meme-coin scandal in which he promoted a token whose price collapsed was dropped on Friday. Lead with who closed it and on what grounds, and what the retail investors who lost money are left with; the mechanism is how a sitting president's endorsement moved a token and why no court will now test it.

stories.label: Marco Rubio calls on Cubans to partner with CIA as Trump vows to 'take care of Cuba'; Cuba mocks US 'desperation'
stories.summary: The US secretary of state openly invited Cubans to work with the CIA, and Trump said Cuba comes 'next' after Iran, while a US oil blockade already starves the island. Lead with the public recruitment call: a regime-change aim stated aloud. Who bears it is 11 million Cubans living with fuel shortages and blackouts; give Havana's reply. Dateline Havana, where the policy lands.

stories.label: Iran steps up plots to kill US diplomats in Middle East
stories.summary: New development in the Gulf war: the US has ordered diplomatic staff out of posts across the Middle East after the director of national intelligence warned of increased Iranian and Houthi plotting against US officials. Departure orders usually come before an escalation. Tie it to Trump's remarks the same day that another operation against Iran may come as the war nears eight months, and give the US claim as a US intelligence claim, not as fact. Name which posts are affected.

stories.label: Arab and Islamic countries call for resumption of traffic in Strait of Hormuz -- statement
stories.summary: The foreign ministers of Egypt, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey jointly demanded that traffic through the Strait of Hormuz resume in full, and said the Iran–Israel–US war must be settled by diplomacy alone. It comes a day after the IRGC said two more supertankers were hit and mines laid. Lead with four Muslim-majority powers, two of them US allies, speaking as a bloc on the shipping lane their economies depend on. Chart ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude. TASS is the only source: attribute the statement to it.

stories.label: Xi orders all-out rescue efforts after 7.0-magnitude quake
stories.summary: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck a county in southwest China, and Xi Jinping ordered an all-out search for the missing. Lead with the county, the toll and the number missing as reported so far; say the figures are early. Only state media carry it (Iran's Mehr, relaying Chinese state reporting), so attribute every figure.

stories.label: Inside Zamfara communities, where residents bear brunt of reprisal attacks by bandits
stories.summary: Ground reporting from Dansadau in Zamfara: after soldiers killed his fighters, the bandit leader Dankarami Gwaska attacked a military base and mining sites on 5 October, and villagers paid for it. Lead with the reprisal cycle, in which each military operation is followed by attacks on civilians who have no protection. Bring in the gold-mining economy that funds the armed groups.

stories.label: Salud promete pagarle a 727 médicos mientras el presidente-ministro está de gira
stories.summary: After 47 days of protest by unpaid doctors, Honduras's health ministry has promised to pay 727 of them, while President Nasry Asfura, who also holds the health portfolio himself, is on a tour of Italy. Lead with the president running the ministry in absentia while public hospitals go without doctors. Patients bear the cost. Dateline Tegucigalpa.

stories.label: Ripple news: Franklin Templeton adds $150 million of money-market shares to XRP Ledger
stories.summary: Franklin Templeton put $150 million of tokenized money-market fund shares onto the XRP Ledger, all of them in a single wallet, and the issuer can approve, freeze or claw back any holding. Lead with that control: 'on-chain' dollar debt that the asset manager can still freeze is a permissioned ledger on a public chain. The mechanism is how tokenized Treasuries are spreading into crypto collateral, and what that means for the claim that crypto is censorship-resistant.

stories.label: 3万亿级参数！Kimi K3.1空降国产第一，1/5价格狙击Astra，实测跑通3D建模
stories.summary: Moonshot AI released Kimi K3.1 Pro, a 3-trillion-parameter model with a 1-million-token context, and will open-source it by 4 November. It ranks fourth on Artificial Analysis, ahead of GPT-6 Astra, at about a fifth of Astra's price ($2/$10 per million tokens against $10/$50). Lead with the open weights at that size and price: a Chinese lab is giving away near-frontier capability that US labs sell. The mechanism is heavily scaled reinforcement-learning post-training. Its Terminal Bench 4.0 score is 65.7% against 66.4% for Claude Opus 5.5.

stories.label: 首部！国产AI超写实电影上院线了
stories.summary: China's first photorealistic AI-generated feature film licensed for cinema release, 'Sanxingdui: Future Past', opened with 301,500 yuan on its first day. Built with Shengshu's Vidu video model and Bona Film, it cost tens of millions of yuan, about 90% less than a comparable live-action sci-fi film. Lead with that gap: costs collapsed, but audiences have not paid. Add the industrial scale: iQiyi plans more than 40 AIGC films this year and Netflix says nearly 300 titles use generative AI.

stories.label: 全线扩产仍供不应求，光刻机被抢疯了
stories.summary: Lithography tools are sold out even as every maker expands capacity, because new investment now covers more lithography steps, from wafer fabrication to advanced packaging, driven by AI chip demand. Lead with the bottleneck and who controls it: ASML at the top, export controls on China, and the Chinese and Japanese makers filling the packaging tier. Use the article's order and capacity figures.

stories.label: Yet two other supertankers hit mines in Hormuz: IRGC
stories.summary: New since the seven tankers Iran claimed on 22 October: the IRGC Navy now says two more 'non-compliant' supertankers struck naval mines off the southern side of the Strait of Hormuz early Friday and their crews abandoned them. This is an Iranian state-media claim (Mehr, TASS relaying) and must be attributed; Al Jazeera's report on the earlier strikes is the independent context. Lead with the mine field as an enforcement tool: Iran is deciding which ships may pass. Name ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude, which Drop Site reports hit $114.

stories.label: First Russian diesel shipment from Putin-Trump deal headed for US -- but it won't arrive before Midterms
stories.summary: The Malta-flagged tanker Agoio Fanades is carrying 40,000 tonnes of Russian ultra-low-sulfur diesel to New York under the Trump-Putin deal; Deputy PM Novak (TASS) says three tankers are already sailing, 500,000 tonnes can go in October, and Rosneft — a sanctioned company — would supply most of it. Lead with the reversal: the country that built the sanctions regime on Russian fuel is now importing it, because a Gulf war has squeezed diesel supply. Datelined at the Russian loading port.

stories.label: New steel plant is early test for Argentina’s big investment scheme
stories.summary: The San Nicolás plant, targeting 360,000 tonnes a year of lower-carbon steel, is the first industrial project — not a mine — to win Milei's RIGI tax-and-currency breaks. Lead with that distinction: RIGI was sold as a magnet for extraction, and this tests whether it can build manufacturing. Distinct from the Taca Taca copper application covered earlier today; say who gives up revenue (provinces, the treasury) for 30 years of guarantees.

stories.label: Melania Trump secures "temporary ceasefire" in Ukrainian city - AOL
stories.summary: The First Lady's office, not the president or State Department, announced a localized ceasefire for Russian-occupied Oleshky on the Dnipro's left bank, a town cut off from food and medicine by constant drone fire. Lead with the residents trapped there and what the pause is meant to let in or out; then the oddity of the channel, and that Kremlin talks in Abu Dhabi are set for November. Dateline Oleshky.

stories.label: 2 ex-FBI officials charged with lying to Congress about Hunter Biden laptop probe
stories.summary: The Justice Department has charged two former FBI officials with lying to Congress about the 2020 Hunter Biden laptop inquiry, eleven days before the midterms; their lawyers say the department is reviving a scandal for the vote. Lead with the timing against DOJ's own long-standing rule of avoiding overt steps near elections, and set it beside the same week's DOJ suit to block Alaska's Senate certification: a pattern of the department acting on the election.

stories.label: Why is Trump questioning Ilhan Omar's name?
stories.summary: A Justice Department court filing listed a different name for Rep. Ilhan Omar, and Trump used it to demand the Somali-born Muslim congresswoman resign, reviving a long-debunked identity-fraud claim. Lead with the mechanism: a government filing turned into a campaign weapon against a sitting member of Congress weeks before her election. Report what the filing actually says and what has been established; Middle East Eye's piece is opinion, use it only as attributed context. Dateline Minneapolis.

stories.label: Organized Crime Postponed Democracy in Haiti, Again
stories.summary: The UN's Carlos Ruiz Massieu told the Security Council on 19 October that Haiti is still far from its first national election since 2016. Lead with the decade without a vote, and the mechanism: gangs such as Viv Ansanm now govern territory, tax roads and decide who can campaign, so the question is no longer when Haiti votes but under whose control. Name who bears it: the displaced in Port-au-Prince.

stories.label: PF acha nota de Willer Tomaz citando indiciado no caso Abin Paralela e “180 mil dólares”
stories.summary: Brazil's Federal Police found a note from lawyer Willer Tomaz, a friend of Flávio Bolsonaro, naming a suspect indicted in the 'parallel Abin' case — the intelligence agency used to spy on Jair Bolsonaro's opponents — alongside '180 mil dólares'. Both deny any link. Lead with the note and the sum, days before the runoff in which Flávio is the candidate; explain the Abin Paralela scheme for readers who missed it. Dateline Brasília.

stories.label: Police admit operatives shot entertainer, give reason
stories.summary: Enugu State police now admit their Anti-Cultism Section shot dead entertainer Izuchukwu Nnaji ('Stone') after hundreds of young people protested Thursday. Lead with the admission and the reason police give, then the pattern: a special tactical unit, an accusation of cultism after the fact, the same shape as the SARS killings that drove #EndSARS in 2020. Who investigates the police is the accountability question. Dateline Enugu.

stories.label: With Strict Agendas and Silent Corridors Kazakhstan’s Kurultai Is Muzzling the Press
stories.summary: Kazakhstan's new unicameral parliament, the Kurultai, has brought in rules that keep journalists from approaching and questioning officials in its corridors, and reporters are pushing back. Lead with what the rules forbid and who made them; the structural point is that Tokayev's 'New Kazakhstan' reform which created the Kurultai is narrowing the press's access to it. Dateline Astana.

stories.label: Counting magnetic flux quanta offers new way to measure photon numbers
stories.summary: Researchers at Japan's AIST directly observed the magnetic flux quanta a superconductor generates when it absorbs photons, and showed the count of flux quanta tells you how many photons arrived. Lead with the principle: a photon-number detector read out as discrete magnetic units, which matters for quantum communication and optical quantum computing, where knowing whether one or two photons arrived is the whole game. Dateline Tsukuba.

stories.label: Updated Google privacy policy says your Gmail might be used for advertising
stories.summary: Google's updated privacy policy says that turning on its 'Personal Intelligence' AI feature lets it use Gmail and other personal data for ad targeting, after years of promising email content would not feed ads. Lead with the reversal and the mechanism: the AI assistant is the consent gate, so opting into a feature opts you into ads. Name the scale — Gmail's billions of accounts.

stories.label: DeepSeek之后，StartLux再来：开源首个决策模型推理引擎，推理快至5.3倍
stories.summary: Two days after DeepSeek open-sourced DeepInfer, the inference framework it runs in production (20 October), the five-month-old Chinese startup StartLux open-sourced Prism, an engine built only for 'decision models' that output a probability over fixed answers rather than text. Lead with the trick: scoring 26 letter options instead of 248,000 tokens cuts the output layer to 0.01%, and int8 integer arithmetic makes results identical regardless of batch order. The structural point: Chinese labs are competing on inference engineering, not model size. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: Robot chipmaker Huixi completes Series B financing led by Beijing AI fund
stories.summary: Huixi Technology, which designs chips for robots, closed Pre-B-plus and Series B rounds led by the Beijing Artificial Intelligence Industry Investment Fund with the Beijing Robotics Industry Development fund alongside. Lead with who is paying: municipal state funds, not private VCs, are leading the round — the mechanism by which Beijing is building a domestic robot-chip supply chain as US export rules tighten. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: One person killed in suspected 'Islamophobic' shooting near Paris
stories.summary: A gunman opened fire in the streets of Trappes and La Verrière west of Paris, killing one and wounding four, and prosecutors are weighing a terrorism inquiry into a suspected anti-Muslim motive. Lead with who was targeted and whether France applies the terrorism label it uses readily for Muslim attackers; Trappes is a heavily Muslim banlieue long cast in political rhetoric as a 'lost territory'.

stories.label: DOJ Sues to Block Alaska Senate Race Certification If GOP Loses
stories.summary: The Justice Department is suing in advance to stop Alaska certifying its Senate result only if the Republican loses, citing 'voter confusion' from two similarly named candidates. Lead with the asymmetry: a federal suit conditioned on one party losing, before a vote is cast, in a seat both parties see as deciding the Senate. The mechanism is pre-emptive litigation as a tool to contest results.

stories.label: Russia-Ukraine talks planned for November in UAE: Kremlin
stories.summary: The Kremlin confirmed US-brokered trilateral talks with Ukraine in Abu Dhabi in November, the first since negotiations stopped earlier this year. Lead with the venue: the UAE as broker between Moscow, Kyiv and Washington. Context: Zelensky's recent openness to a frozen front line and the drone wave on Moscow; prediction markets have priced a NATO-Russia clash by month's end up from 6% to 21% this week, after a drone sank a ship off Constanta.

stories.label: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia have completed ratification of Makkah defence pact: FO
stories.summary: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have ratified the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement signed with Türkiye in August, and Ankara is part way through ratifying it. Lead with what ratification binds: a nuclear-armed state, the Gulf's largest oil producer and NATO's second-largest army in a mutual-defence pact, as drones hit Saudi energy sites and Riyadh fights the Houthis again. Explain what the pact obliges each party to do if one is attacked.

stories.label: Khartoum courts UN-backed relief to stave off truce pressure; Tasis govt heedful after health minister’s angry exit; Abyei strike tests Juba ties; Drones hit RSF, military’s seats of power; RSF pushes in Kurmuk, military wins Geisan ground
stories.summary: Drones struck Khartoum, Nyala, a gold mine in South Kordofan, a West Kordofan town and a White Nile power station this week, killing hundreds. Both the army and the RSF blame neighbours for letting the drones through. Lead with the civilian toll and the infrastructure lost (power, gold, homes), then the mechanism: Khartoum courting UN-backed relief to deflect truce pressure, a strike in Abyei straining ties with Juba, and the RSF advance on Kurmuk at the Ethiopian border.

stories.label: Brazil inflation shoots through target limit before runoff vote
stories.summary: Brazil's inflation broke through the upper limit of the central bank's target days before the Lula–Flávio Bolsonaro runoff. Lead with the figure and what drove it (food, fuel and the oil shock from the Gulf war), then who pays: low-income households, Lula's base. Context from Al Jazeera: Bolsonaro's party already gained in Congress, so whoever wins inherits rising prices and a hostile legislature. This is not the Meta AI bias story already covered.

stories.label: First Quantum readies Argentina tax-break plans for $5.3 billion Taca Taca copper project
stories.summary: First Quantum will apply before year-end for Argentina's RIGI large-investment incentive regime for Taca Taca, a $5.25 billion copper project and one of the world's largest undeveloped deposits. Lead with what RIGI gives away (tax, customs and FX guarantees fixed for 30 years) and who gives it: Milei's state, in exchange for copper demanded by data centres and EVs. Tie it to copper prices; First Quantum is the company that lost its Panama mine.

stories.label: Chart: A record two-thirds of car sales in China are now electric vehicles
stories.summary: New-energy vehicles were 67% of China's new car sales in September, a record. Lead with that number and what it does to oil: the world's largest car market stops growing its petrol demand just as Gulf supply is under attack and Brent crude climbs. Name who loses (oil exporters, foreign carmakers in China) and who gains.

stories.label: Crows can evaluate visual info twice as fast as mammals
stories.summary: In the classic random-dot-motion decision task, crows reached judgments about twice as fast as monkeys. Lead with the speed and the mechanism: a compact, densely packed bird brain without a layered neocortex. The surprise is that decades of decision neuroscience built on primates may have mistaken one brain architecture for the general rule.

stories.label: Novartis multiple sclerosis treatment cuts rates of relapse in pivotal trials
stories.summary: In pivotal trials, Novartis's oral BTK inhibitor remibrutinib cut multiple sclerosis relapses by a third against teriflunomide, a standard pill. Lead with the result and the trade-off: it is less effective than Roche's rival BTK drug but has a better safety profile. BTK inhibitors are the first new MS drug class in years, so a liver-safety advantage can decide which one patients get.

stories.label: Intel gets waiver after worries fuzzy US ban on foreign-made robots may hit fabs
stories.summary: The FCC's ban on foreign-made robots was so loosely drawn that Intel, the US chip champion, had to request a waiver to keep the automated guided vehicles that move wafers in its fabs. The same week the FCC banned a video transmitter and a dashcam built on Huawei HiSilicon surveillance chips (The Record). Lead with the irony: an industrial policy meant to protect US chipmaking first had to exempt the US chipmaker, because its fabs run on foreign automation.

stories.label: SA's Presidency website taken down as cybersecurity flaw sparks warnings across the world
stories.summary: A new development in the PHP2Shell flaw already covered: governments are now taking their own sites offline. South Africa's Presidency went dark citing a 'global cybersecurity event', joining the port of Rotterdam, Belgium's foreign ministry and Finnish public services. Lead with the state, not the cloud firms: a flaw in the language under most of the web is forcing governments to choose between going offline and being breached, and poorer administrations with slower patch cycles carry more of the exposure.

stories.label: KI-Boom: Wie die Bundesregierung die Regulierung von Rechenzentren aushöhlt
stories.summary: As AI drives data-centre power demand up, the German government plans to weaken the energy-efficiency and waste-heat rules in its own Energy Efficiency Act rather than enforce them, after Merz courted Nvidia's Jensen Huang at an 'Invest in Germany' summit. Lead with which rules are being cut (efficiency thresholds, waste-heat reuse) and who asked for it: the largest US tech companies. The mechanism: Europe's strictest data-centre law is being loosened to win investment.

stories.label: Romania blames Russia as drone strike sinks ship, kills sailor
stories.summary: A drone strike sank a civilian cargo ship off Romania's Black Sea coast near Constanța and killed a sailor — a NATO member's waters, a dead crewman, a sunk hull. Lead with the sinking and the sailor. Mechanism: Russian strikes on Ukraine's Danube and Black Sea export routes now land inside NATO territory, and President Nicusor Dan calls it deliberate escalation on the eastern flank; say what Romania is asking of NATO (Article 4 or not) and what it means for grain shipping out of the Black Sea.

stories.label: Seven killed as gunmen open fire near Christian church in Jordan -- TV
stories.summary: Gunmen opened fire on a funeral procession outside a Christian church in Al-Karak, killing at least seven; they did not get inside, where more than 150 mourners had gathered. Only Russian state agency TASS carries it, citing a Jordanian security source speaking to Arab TV — attribute every figure ('TASS reported, citing a security source') and do not state the toll as fact. Lead with the mourners killed; give the context of Karak's old Christian community and Jordan's record of attacks there (the 2016 Karak castle attack), and what Amman has confirmed.

stories.label: Ron and Yuval fell killed in shooting attack near Hebron
stories.summary: Material new development on the Hebron arc: two Israeli soldiers were killed and three people wounded at a checkpoint near Hebron, and the two Palestinian gunmen were killed. Count and name all four dead with equal weight. Mechanism: this comes the day after Hebron was put under lockdown and Ben-Gvir called for dismantling the Palestinian Authority — say what collective measures (closures, raids, demolitions) the army has announced for Hebron's 200,000+ Palestinians, and that every source here is Israeli or US.

stories.label: Republican 'Muslim Brotherhood' attacks on Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan seek to exploit Democratic fault lines
stories.summary: Less than two weeks before the 3 November midterms, Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers and President Trump — who falsely called him a 'jihadist' — are tying Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, a Muslim physician and epidemiologist, to the Muslim Brotherhood. Lead with the president's word and that it is false. Mechanism: the attack aims at Michigan's Democratic split over Gaza, trying to peel off pro-Israel and moderate voters while Arab and Muslim voters weigh turnout; say what polls show and what a Muslim senator from Michigan would mean. Public attention is high (El-Sayed is trending).

stories.label: PM Shehbaz sets indicative wheat price at Rs4,500 per maund for 2027
stories.summary: Pakistan raised its indicative wheat price for the 2027 crop by Rs1,000 to Rs4,500 per maund (40 kg), citing production costs — a 29% rise that reaches every household through flour. Lead with the number and who pays: farmers get a floor after the 2024-25 procurement collapse left them selling below cost, while urban consumers face dearer atta. Mechanism: the IMF programme pushed Islamabad out of guaranteed procurement, so explain whether the state will actually buy at this price. Name wheat prices and compare to world wheat.

stories.label: Ruble slowing down amid Russian regulator's decision to keep key rate
stories.summary: The Bank of Russia held its key rate at 14% on Friday, and the ruble's climb stalled (yuan at about 12.04 rubles). Russian state agency TASS is the only source — attribute it. Lead with the rate decision, not the tick: a war economy keeping borrowing costs at 14% to hold down inflation while oil prices rise. Mechanism: a strong ruble cuts the budget's ruble take from oil exports, so say who gains and who loses from the hold. Name the ruble and Brent crude.

stories.label: Hong Kong burnishes gold hub credentials with local refineries deal
stories.summary: Hong Kong signed deals for gold refineries, including Switzerland's Valcambi, to localise production in the city, completing a trading-refining-vaulting chain. Lead with who is moving: Swiss refiners setting up next to the world's largest gold buyer. Mechanism: central banks led by China are buying gold to hold reserves outside dollar sanctions, and a full Hong Kong chain lets that bullion move without passing through London or Zurich. Name gold prices.

stories.label: Why is Moderna stock sliding today? By Investing.com
stories.summary: Phase 3 results for intismeran autogene, the personalised mRNA melanoma vaccine Moderna and Merck give alongside Keytruda, were disclosed before their scheduled presentation, and Moderna shares collapsed. Lead with the trial result itself — did the vaccine cut melanoma recurrence or death against Keytruda alone, and by how much — then why investors read it as a disappointment. Mechanism: each patient's vaccine is built from their own tumour's mutations; this is the first Phase 3 test of whether that works at scale. Keep the stock to one line.

stories.label: Suppressor tRNAs restore functionally enhanced tumour suppressor protein to induce tumour regression
stories.summary: Engineered 'suppressor' tRNAs read through the premature stop signals that truncate tumour-suppressor genes such as TP53, restoring a working — even enhanced — protein and shrinking tumours. Lead with the regression. Mechanism: nonsense mutations cause roughly one in ten inherited disease cases and many cancers, and one tRNA could in principle fix the same stop codon in any gene; say what model it worked in and how far it is from patients.

stories.label: Brazil presidential election dogged by alleged bias by Meta AI tools | New Scientist
stories.summary: Days before Sunday's tied Lula–Flávio Bolsonaro runoff, Lula's camp accuses Meta of making its AI tools generate campaign content for Bolsonaro more readily than for Lula. Lead with the specific test or evidence of the asymmetry. Mechanism: in a WhatsApp-first electorate, a platform's generator defaults become campaign infrastructure, and Brazil's electoral court (TSE) has rules on AI content — say what it has done and what Meta answers.

stories.label: Beschwerde erfolgreich: Politisches Microtargeting von vier Parteien war rechtswidrig
stories.summary: Berlin's data protection commissioner ruled that at least four German parties broke the law by microtargeting Facebook ads at chosen groups of voters in the 2021 Bundestag campaign. Lead with the ruling and name the parties. Mechanism: targeting on inferred political views uses 'special category' data under the GDPR, which needs explicit consent — a precedent for how parties everywhere in the EU buy ads on Meta, and it lands as the EU's political-ad regulation takes effect. Say what penalty, if any, follows.

stories.label: Audi reportedly seeks Huawei platform for next-generation A8 built in China
stories.summary: Audi is in talks to build the China version of its flagship A8 on Huawei's vehicle architecture, made in China with Huawei doing the key development, Manager Magazin reports. Lead with the reversal: a German luxury flagship running on a Chinese tech company's platform. Mechanism: in the world's largest car market, software, cockpit and driver-assist now sell the car, and Huawei's HIMA stack is ahead of what Volkswagen Group builds — tell it from the mainland tech press's view of who now supplies whom.
